entities.name: PMID:27490767
observations: Queensland population linkage study of 4,104 women undergoing mastectomy for localized invasive breast cancer, diagnosed 1997–2012; reconstruction overall 11.7%. Authors reported that geographic disparity reduced significantly over time, although reconstruction remained more likely in high-accessibility and less disadvantaged areas.

entities.name: PMID:41924348
observations: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 15 studies with 46,986 rural and 1,833,906 urban mastectomy patients; rural patients had lower odds of immediate reconstruction (OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.57–0.79; I²=97%). Meta-regression found no temporal trend in rural–urban disparity.

entities.name: Queensland gap narrowed
observations: A population-based Queensland study of diagnoses from 1997–2012 reported a significant reduction over time in geographic disparity in postmastectomy breast reconstruction; residual access and socioeconomic differences remained.

entities.name: Rural reconstruction gap persists
observations: A meta-analysis of 15 international studies found rural patients had 33% lower odds of immediate reconstruction than urban patients (OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.57–0.79) and no detectable temporal trend in the gap; heterogeneity was high (I²=97%).
